---
title: "Composable Pipeline"
---

R7/S7-based composable pipeline framework for building custom analysis
workflows.

::: {.callout-note}
The composable pipeline requires the [S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/)
package (listed in `Suggests`). Install it with `install.packages("S7")`.
:::

## Core classes

### `sw_pipeline_step` {#sw_pipeline_step}

Create a processing step.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_step(name, FUN, ARGS = list())
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Character string — step name. |
| `FUN` | Function to execute. |
| `ARGS` | Named list of additional arguments (default: empty list). |

#### Details

Constructs a `ProcessingStep` S7 object. When executed, `FUN` is called as:
`do.call(FUN, c(list(previous_result), ARGS))`.

#### Value

A `ProcessingStep` S7 object.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_run` {#sw_pipeline_step_run}

Execute a single processing step.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_step_run(step, input)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `step` | A `ProcessingStep` object. |
| `input` | Input data (passed as first argument to the step's function). |

#### Details

If the step declares an `input_type`, `input` must satisfy `methods::is()` for at least one declared class. Otherwise the call stops with a "type check failed" error before the step function runs. Steps with no `input_type` are not checked. Every runner, including the `targets` backend, goes through this check.

The error from a direct call names the step only. `sw_pipeline_run()` and `sw_pipeline_run_targets()` add the pipeline name and step position, so both runners give the same message. The generated `targets` command contains neither, so renaming a pipeline or moving a step does not rebuild cached targets. Upgrading from the previous release does not rebuild existing `targets` stores for this change: the generated command text is the same as before.

#### Value

The result of calling `step@FUN(input, ...)`.

---

### `sw_pipeline` {#sw_pipeline}

Create a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline(name, steps = NULL)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Character string — pipeline name. |
| `steps` | Optional list of `ProcessingStep` objects. |

#### Value

A `Pipeline` S7 object.

---

## Pipeline operations

### `sw_pipeline_add` {#sw_pipeline_add}

Add a step to a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_add(pipeline, step, after = NULL)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `pipeline` | A `Pipeline` object. |
| `step` | A `ProcessingStep` to add. |
| `after` | Optional position after which to insert (default: append at end). |

#### Value

A new `Pipeline` object with the step added.

---

### `sw_pipeline_remove` {#sw_pipeline_remove}

Remove a step from a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_remove(pipeline, name_or_index)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `pipeline` | A `Pipeline` object. |
| `name_or_index` | Step name (character) or index (integer) to remove. |

#### Value

A new `Pipeline` object with the step removed.

---

### `sw_pipeline_replace` {#sw_pipeline_replace}

Replace a step in a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_replace(pipeline, name_or_index, new_step)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `pipeline` | A `Pipeline` object. |
| `name_or_index` | Step name or index to replace. |
| `new_step` | The new `ProcessingStep` object. |

#### Value

A new `Pipeline` object with the step replaced.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_names` {#sw_pipeline_step_names}

Get step names from a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_step_names(pipeline)
```

#### Value

Character vector of step names.

---

### `sw_pipeline_length` {#sw_pipeline_length}

Get the number of steps in a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_length(pipeline)
```

#### Value

Integer.

---

### `sw_pipeline_run` {#sw_pipeline_run}

Execute a pipeline.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_run(pipeline, input, trace = TRUE)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `pipeline` | A `Pipeline` object. |
| `input` | Initial input data for the first step. |
| `trace` | Logical; whether to print progress messages (default: `TRUE`). |

#### Details

Runs all steps in order, threading data from one step to the next. If a step
fails, execution stops and the error is reported with the step name.

#### Value

A named list with: `result` (final output), `intermediates` (named list of
per-step results), `steps_completed` (integer count).

---

### `sw_pipeline_concat` {#sw_pipeline_concat}

Concatenate two pipelines.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_concat(pipeline1, pipeline2, name = NULL)
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `pipeline1` | First `Pipeline` object. |
| `pipeline2` | Second `Pipeline` object. |
| `name` | Optional name for the new pipeline. |

#### Value

A new `Pipeline` object containing all steps from both pipelines.

---

### `sw_pipeline_show` {#sw_pipeline_show}

Print a pipeline summary.

#### Usage

```r
sw_pipeline_show(pipeline)
```

#### Details

Displays a human-readable summary of the pipeline and its steps. Called for
its side effect of printing.

#### Value

Invisible `NULL`.

---

### `sw_plot_pipeline` {#sw_plot_pipeline}

Plot pipeline processing queue.

#### Usage

```r
sw_plot_pipeline(pipeline, style = c("text", "data"))
```

#### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `pipeline` | A `Pipeline` object. |
| `style` | Output style: `"text"` (flowchart printed to console) or `"data"` (returns a data.frame). |

#### Details

Renders a text-based flowchart of the pipeline steps, showing the sequential
flow of data through each processing step.

#### Value

For `style = "text"`, invisible `NULL`. For `style = "data"`, a `data.frame`
with columns `step_number`, `name`, `n_args`.

---

## Pre-built step constructors

Convenience constructors that create `ProcessingStep` objects wrapping
SpectraWeaveR functions.

### `sw_pipeline_step_read_fcs` {#sw_pipeline_step_read_fcs}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_read_fcs(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_io_read_fcs()`. Additional arguments are passed via
`ARGS`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_filter_margins` {#sw_pipeline_step_filter_margins}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_filter_margins(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_filter_margins()`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_qc` {#sw_pipeline_step_qc}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_qc(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_qc_run()`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_correct` {#sw_pipeline_step_correct}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_correct(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_correct_run()`. Pass `design_audit` (an `sw_design_audit` or `NULL` for an explicit skip); the step stops when it runs without it.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_normalize` {#sw_pipeline_step_normalize}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_normalize(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_correct_normalize()`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_som` {#sw_pipeline_step_som}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_som(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_correct_som()`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_correct_apply` {#sw_pipeline_step_correct_apply}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_correct_apply(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_correct_apply()`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_cluster` {#sw_pipeline_step_cluster}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_cluster(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_cluster_run()`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_design_audit` {#sw_pipeline_step_design_audit}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_design_audit(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_design_audit()`. Input is the sample table, output an `sw_design_audit`. Pass `minimum_batches`, `minimum_batches_origin` and `require_shared_reference` in `...`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_batch_decide` {#sw_pipeline_step_batch_decide}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_batch_decide(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_batch_decide()`. Input is an `sw_design_audit`, output an `sw_batch_decision`. Pass `candidates`, `policy`, `identity_id`, `label_source` and `contrast_records` in `...`.

---

### `sw_pipeline_step_flag_iqr` {#sw_pipeline_step_flag_iqr}

```r
sw_pipeline_step_flag_iqr(...)
```

Creates a step wrapping `sw_flag_iqr()`. Input is the event-level data frame, output an `sw_flag_iqr` tibble. Every threshold, the multiplier and `min_effect` go in `...`.

---

## Example

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(SpectraWeaveR)

# Build a custom pipeline
pipe <- sw_pipeline("my-qc-pipeline")
pipe <- sw_pipeline_add(pipe, sw_pipeline_step_filter_margins())
pipe <- sw_pipeline_add(pipe, sw_pipeline_step_qc())

# Inspect it
sw_pipeline_show(pipe)
sw_plot_pipeline(pipe)

# Run it
result <- sw_pipeline_run(pipe, input = my_flowframe)
result$result           # final cleaned flowFrame
result$intermediates    # per-step outputs
```
